title: Reported and Indirect Speech
summary: Report what someone said by adjusting pronouns, time words, and verb tenses.

sections.heading: Basic reporting with que
sections.body: Use reporting verbs such as **dizer**, **falar**, **explicar**, **perguntar**, and **responder** followed by **que** for statements.

examples.en: She said that she was tired.

examples.pt: O professor explicou que a prova seria curta.
examples.en: The teacher explained that the test would be short.

sections.heading: Tense and time shifts
sections.body: When reporting from a past point of view, present often becomes imperfect, future becomes conditional, and hoje/amanhã may become naquele dia/no dia seguinte.

examples.pt: Ele falou que morava em Santos.
examples.en: He said he lived in Santos.

examples.pt: Ela disse que ligaria no dia seguinte.
examples.en: She said she would call the next day.
They warned that they were arriving.

sections.heading: Reported questions and requests
sections.body: Indirect questions use question words or **se** for yes/no questions. Requests often use **pedir para + infinitive** or **pedir que + subjunctive**.

examples.pt: Ele perguntou onde ficava o banheiro.
examples.en: He asked where the bathroom was.

examples.pt: Ela perguntou se eu podia ajudar.
examples.en: She asked if I could help.

keyPoints: Reported statements usually use dizer/falar que.
Past reporting often shifts present to imperfect and future to conditional.
Requests can use pedir para + infinitive or pedir que + subjunctive.

commonMistakes.note: From a past reporting point, shift to imperfect.

commonMistakes.wrong: Ele perguntou que eu queria café.
commonMistakes.right: Ele perguntou se eu queria café.
commonMistakes.note: Use se for yes/no indirect questions.
Use para before the infinitive subject.
